stories.title: A Stanford professor posts an all-human rival Riemann proof, and AI helps flag problems in it
stories.summary: Ravi Vakil, Stanford mathematician and AMS president, posted Alessandro Masullo's draft proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis: 'It is all human, with no AI.' About eight hours later he said people had reported problems in it, identified with the assistance of different AI models.

predictions.note: AI models helped mathematicians flag problems in a months-reviewed proof draft within about eight hours of its release.

stories.title: Claude's claimed Riemann proof would top 250,000 pages if printed
stories.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude's argument would run to over 250,000 printed pages, so he released it only as Lean code a computer can check, in 14 data packages. The claim has not yet been verified.

stories.title: NYU and Anthropic mathematicians claim an AI-aided Navier-Stokes proof without OpenAI's loophole
stories.summary: Tristan Buckmaster of NYU and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge posted an AI-aided proof that the Navier-Stokes fluid equations can blow up without the 'finely tuned force' in OpenAI's September proof. It is a claim, posted unpolished, and its certificate had not been released.

predictions.note: A second claimed AI-aided proof on a $1 million Millennium problem in a single week, still awaiting its certificate.

stories.title: Two AI models score a perfect 450 on Korea's college entrance exam in a student's test
stories.summary: In tests run by student Gu Yu-gyeom through the models' APIs right after this year's questions were released, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Google's Gemini 4 Neon both scored 450 out of 450, according to Aju Press. It is not an official score.

stories.title: After 100+ cheating cases, Korean universities tighten exam rules and Seoul National hands out its own pens
stories.summary: More than 100 cheating cases were found in this year's entrance exam amid concerns over AI and hidden devices. Seoul National University will provide applicants' writing materials, Sogang warned against clothes with buttons and Sungkyunkwan restricted hats and hoodies.

stories.title: Hidden cameras, tiny earpieces and AI: high-tech exam cheating reaches Australia
stories.summary: The ABC found tiny wireless earpieces and cameras disguised as buttons, pens, water bottles and car keys on sale online, where a few hundred dollars buys a cheating set-up. Macquarie University's Kane Murdoch says such tools have reached Australian exam halls.

stories.title: Australia reviews competition law for AI shopping agents and surveillance pricing
stories.summary: Assistant minister Andrew Leigh said the government is checking whether competition laws keep pace as more consumers shop with AI agents: 'We don't want Australians mucked around by surveillance pricing, powered by AI.'

stories.title: A $30 million LA mansion will take Anthropic or OpenAI shares instead of cash
stories.summary: Developer Phillip Braunstein has listed his Brentwood home for $29,995,000 and says he would accept equity in Anthropic or OpenAI as payment.

stories.title: An 'employees-only' Anthropic hoodie is listed on eBay for $1,800
stories.summary: After Anthropic's IPO, eBay sellers listed Anthropic and Claude items, including a hoodie its seller calls employees-only, with a $1,800 buy-now price, and a $100 Claude tote bag. Anthropic doesn't sell merchandise.

stories.title: A tiny ChatGPT now runs on a 35-year-old Super Nintendo
stories.summary: Tech writer Benj Edwards built ChatGPT for SNES, a 2.2-million-parameter model distilled from OpenAI's GPT-OSS-120b that knows about 8,000 words and often gets things wrong. He designed it; AI coding agents wrote the software.

predictions.note: A human set the goals and design while AI agents wrote the code, but it is one hobby project, not production software.

stories.title: UN killer-robot talks end with 128 countries agreeing only to 'elaborate' rules within two years
stories.summary: At the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva, 128 countries agreed to elaborate a possible accord on lethal autonomous weapons in the next two years. Nearly 100 nations wanted swift binding rules; the US, Russia and Israel opposed them, and Human Rights Watch said 'the technology is racing ahead'.

predictions.note: 128 countries agreed to elaborate an accord on autonomous weapons within two years, but key arms producers opposed binding rules.

stories.title: FaceyBot, a lifelike robot face, will train Singapore care and service staff in tough conversations
stories.summary: Straits Interactive is bringing FaceyBot, a silicone-faced robot with more than a dozen major expressions and hundreds of subtler ones, to eldercare and customer-service trainees from early 2027, priced from $10,000.

stories.title: Zoox's robotaxis with no steering wheel start rolling in Santa Monica
stories.summary: Amazon-owned Zoox put its purpose-built robotaxis, with no steering wheel or pedals and seats facing each other, on the road in Santa Monica for employees and their friends and families; a public wait list opens next year.

stories.title: The University of California signs a systemwide OpenAI deal as faculty urge caution
stories.summary: The deal gives hundreds of thousands of UC students, faculty and staff access to ChatGPT; faculty leaders said they had asked the administration to move with more caution.

stories.title: Oracle says its OpenAI infrastructure contract is fully funded
stories.summary: Oracle said its infrastructure contract with OpenAI is fully funded following a final capital raise earlier this month, according to Reuters.

transcript.t: This is the Singularity Daily, for Sunday, November 22.
Here are the last 24 hours in superintelligence, in 3 minutes.
Show your work. Hours after Claude's claimed Riemann proof, a Stanford professor posted an all-human rival.
Within about eight hours, people using AI models had flagged problems in it.
Printed out, the Anthropic mathematician's proof with Claude would top 250,000 pages.
This week, he and an NYU professor also posted an AI-aided proof about how fluids swirl.
Over in Korea, two AI models scored a perfect 450 on this year's college entrance exam.
After more than 100 cheating cases, Seoul National University will hand out its own pens.
Here in Australia, the ABC found cheating kits online, button cameras and tiny earpieces, for a few hundred dollars.
Canberra's eyeing AI shopping agents too.
Andrew Leigh doesn't want Australians mucked around by surveillance pricing.
Oh, and in LA, a $30 million mansion will take Anthropic or OpenAI shares instead of cash.
And on eBay, an 'employees-only' Anthropic hoodie is listed at $1,800.
Meanwhile, a tech writer squeezed a tiny ChatGPT onto a 35-year-old Super Nintendo.
It knows about 8,000 words, often gets things wrong, and AI agents wrote its code.
The catch? At UN killer-robot talks, 128 countries agreed only to keep talking.
Human Rights Watch says the technology is racing ahead.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
In Singapore, a robot face with hundreds of expressions will help trainees practise tough conversations.
Why not a screen?
"A physical face creates real emotional pressure," says its Singapore backer.
And this week in Santa Monica, Zoox robotaxis with no steering wheel started giving staff rides.
Proofs, exams, robots: the same rule as school. Show your work.
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
Somehow, the future keeps landing early.
That's one day of news. Imagine what a year looks like.
This has been the Singularity Daily.
Same time tomorrow?
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
